Which programme — above the nav, because both surfaces read it

metadata.comment: ABOVE the nav and never inside a surface (L137). Both surfaces read what it chooses, and a copy on each is two controls over one piece of state; the sprint-39 version put it on one tab only, and on the tab named after the programme there was no way to say which programme you were reading.

nodes.label: Surface A — their programme, as they read it

metadata.comment: `mounted`: the surface a coach is not reading does not exist, so nothing in it runs (L119's <details> finding).

THE SAME CHART THE LEARNER READS (L127 §6): the same kit node, the same series, the same par line. Only the headline above it is addressed to a different reader, composed by Logic/Standing from the coach's words. No width/sizeMode here: a kit node's root gets an empty style, so they would be discarded in silence (sprint 45) — the kit stylesheet sizes it.

nodes.label: One row per objective, then their own confidence
The thread — their programme's rows and nothing else

metadata.comment: Holds the repeater and NOTHING else, so its Nth child is the Nth row — which is how a jump from the log finds a row without the row carrying an id in its DOM. Putting one there would change the learner's page, which must stay byte-identical (criterion 11).

nodes.label: Their programme, row for row — the SAME Course/Timeline row the learner's page places

metadata.comment: ONE component, two audiences — never a copy (TASK-L165 §3, L127 §6). In the product this is StaffProgramme rendering PathList in mode="staff". What the audience changes is only about writes and routes: no ask control, and a message draws. The order, the fold and the grouping are L116's and L130's, shared; tools/check-learner-page.mjs fails if a second timeline-row component appears or either page stops placing this one.

nodes.label: Show only — absent when there is only one kind

metadata.comment: A wrapping row of content-sized chips is the intent, not a grid: the uncollapsible-multi-column warning is answered here the way L164 answered it for the cohort pills and sprint 44 for the lesson stepper.

nodes.label: One chip per kind they have
The log — in the model's order, not newest first

metadata.comment: THE ORDER IS THE MODEL'S. The task doc says newest-first; the product's own feed renders the model's order as a recorded deviation, because a coach and their client must not disagree about the shape of the fortnight (TimelineFeed.tsx, L119 criterion 1). Ported rather than re-decided.

metadata.comment: The head is about the person NOW, whichever programme is being read below it (the product's Head reads the live timeline, not the scope). The same component as the one above, over the live entries: one owner of the order, two inputs.

nodes.label: Pace and trajectory, in the coach's words
Which row the log is pointing at

metadata.comment: Runs on the signal ONLY. Since NDA-017 §2, wiring Run no longer makes a Function's value inputs passive — each has its own Run On Value Change box, ticked by default — so without these unticked it also ran whenever a row's id arrived: opening a row in the log jumped to the programme (measured, TASK-L165).
